expectations.text: Claude places bonds (BND) in the Traditional 401k, explaining that bond interest is taxed as ordinary income and sheltering it in a tax-deferred account is the primary benefit
expectations.evidence: Response explicitly states 'BND (bonds) → Traditional 401(k)' and explains 'Bond interest is taxed as ordinary income — at your full marginal rate' and 'The Traditional 401(k) defers all taxes until withdrawal, so it is the ideal shelter for the asset class most punished by current taxation. Put the inefficient asset in the tax-deferred account.'

expectations.text: Claude places international stocks (VXUS) in the taxable account to capture the foreign tax credit, which is lost when international funds are held in tax-advantaged accounts
expectations.evidence: Response states 'VXUS (international stocks) → Taxable brokerage' and explains 'If VXUS is held inside a Traditional 401(k) or Roth IRA, that foreign tax credit is permanently lost. The IRA or 401(k) wrapper cannot pass the FTC through to you.'

expectations.text: Claude places US stocks (VTI) in the Roth IRA as the highest-expected-growth asset that benefits most from never being taxed
expectations.evidence: Response states 'VTI (US stocks) → Roth IRA' and explains 'The fundamental rule of Roth placement: put your highest-expected-return asset here, because you want maximum growth in the account where growth is never taxed. Stocks have higher expected returns than bonds over the long run, so stocks belong in Roth.'

expectations.text: Claude notes the caveat: asset allocation (the right ratio of stocks to bonds) comes first; tax placement is a secondary optimization that only matters if the allocation is already correct
expectations.evidence: Response explicitly states 'Asset location is a second-order optimization. Get your asset allocation right first — the right stock/bond ratio, the right amount of international — and then use placement to extract a bit more efficiency. Don't let the tax-placement tail wag the asset-allocation dog.'

expectations.text: Claude does NOT recommend putting bonds in the Roth IRA or international stocks in the 401k without explaining the tradeoff
expectations.evidence: Response never recommends bonds in the Roth IRA — it actively warns against it: 'The point is not to put bonds in your Roth — that is the canonical mistake: wasting Roth space on a low-growth asset whose returns would have been sheltered anyway in the 401(k).' International stocks in the 401k is also never recommended.
